summary: Summit tower in Los Padres National Forest; sources disagree on the build date (1934 to 1952); staffed into the 1990s, now abandoned and in poor condition.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cab on an 11-foot timber tower, with the lower enclosed room built inside the tower frame
facts.status_note: Still standing, but abandoned for years and in poor condition; no longer used as a lookout

access.note: A forest road reaches the summit, typically open April to November per a 2011 blog; the 2008 photo report says the road has no gate. The tower itself is abandoned and in poor condition.

visit.trail_note: Steep dirt road about 7 miles from the Chuchupate Ranger Station; the tower is abandoned and in poor condition, so climbing it is not advised

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

events.note: December 7, 1920 newspaper item places Mrs. Mary Smith in a station on the summit; register says a lookout was there before 1920
February 1932: the lookout station was described as offering food, sleeping accommodations and stoves for rescue parties searching for a lost airliner
Newspaper delivery by air from a Varney Airlines pilot began July 7, 1932 per a Forest Service bulletin
Laine Davis and his wife were at the station during the 1933 fire season
Register Built field gives 1934; a 2008 photo report says the structure may have been built in 1934
Laine Davis assigned to the station for the 1934 season
Register description says the current structure was constructed in 1943; conflicts with the 1934 Built field
Ridge Route museum says an earlier building burned down in 1952; Desert Explorers says a fire destroyed the original structure
Current wooden tower brought in from Santa Barbara to replace the burned building in 1952, per the museum; Desert Explorers says it was built in 1936 in Santa Barbara County
August 1956 fire at the peak reported by lookout Lee Hartley; held to about 50 acres
Tom Fusek came to the lookout in 1985 and was spending five days a week in the tower room by 1990
Approximate: two later pages say lookout use ended in the 1990s; a September 1990 Los Angeles Times article said closure might follow that fire season
Photo report dated August 3, 2008 says the lookout has been abandoned for some years and is in bad shape

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field and a 2011 blog give 1934, and a 2008 photo report says the structure may date from 1934, with a building there in 1926. The register's own description says the current structure went up in 1943. A 2017 museum post and a 2021 trip report put the present tower's arrival at 1952 after an earlier building burned; the 2021 report says the wooden tower was built in 1936. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick one date.
The register gives 8,027 ft (2,447 m). The Ridge Route museum and a 1990 Los Angeles Times article give 8,013 ft. The story says about 8,000 feet.

notes_for_editor: Build date is contested and the story says so; the record's built 1934 is the register's Built field, but its own description dates the current structure to 1943, and other pages say 1936 build with 1952 move. Editor may want to add a 1943 or 1952 event after review. Closure after the 1990 season is not confirmed: sources read say lookout use ended 'in the 1990s' and the 1990 Los Angeles Times article raised a possible closure, but nothing read gives the exact year or a Forest Service notice. A search result pointed to a Los Padres graphic saying the last tower used there was 1990; not read, so not used. Access level 'public' rests on a 2008 photo report and a 2011 blog, not a Forest Service notice; check with the Los Padres National Forest before relying on it. The 'climbable: false' value is editorial, drawn from the 2008 report's 'bad shape' wording; no source says climbing is forbidden, and the story gives the advice as the writer's own. The 1958 closure for winter and the 1956 Ground Observer Corps post were noted but left out for length. No new photos added.
